title: Roo and Hazel's Warm Blanket
markdown:
The air grew soft and cool. It whispered secrets through the leaves in the meadow. Roo the little mouse wiggled his nose. He felt a gentle shiver. It was not a cold shiver. It felt like summer was waving goodbye. Beside him, Hazel the hare listened. Her long ears drooped a little. She heard the wind’s soft song.

“Oh, Hazel,” squeaked Roo, his voice like a tiny bell. “The wind sounds a little colder today, doesn’t it? Like it’s getting ready to blow cold winds.”

Hazel nodded. Her nose twitched. Her long ears moved to hear every sound. “It does, little Roo. And I heard Farmer Giles say Sion the scarecrow is feeling chilly. His straw filling isn’t as warm and puffy as it used to be. The wind blows right through him, feeling a little sharp.”

Roo’s shiny eyes grew wide. Sion was a friendly scarecrow. He always waved his straw arms. He was a quiet friend. The thought of him feeling cold made Roo’s little heart feel a tiny bit sad, like a little grey cloud.

“Oh dear me,” he whispered, his small voice fluttering. “We must do something. Sion needs to be warm and cozy. He needs a warm hug.”

Hazel’s long ears perked up. She had bright bouncy ideas. Her whole body wiggled with gentle excitement. “A wonderful thought, Roo. What if we made him a little blanket? A very soft, very warm blanket, to keep him snug when the wind blows his straw about.”

Roo bounced on his little paws. His tail gave a happy flick. “Yes. A blanket. A warm blanket. Just for Sion.”

So the two friends, Roo and Hazel, with their kind hearts and big ideas, went on their gentle quest. They looked for the softest, warmest things in the meadow. Roo, being so small and quick, ran into an old picnic basket near the woods. Inside he found a warm and fuzzy piece of yarn the colour of a gentle sunrise, with soft pinks and pale yellow. It felt soft like a fluffy cloud. Hazel, with her long strong legs, hopped to a sunny spot. Fluffy white bits from dandelions were ready to float on the breeze. She gathered a handful of the softest fluffiest seeds, light as wishes.

“This yarn will be just right for wrapping him up, won’t it, Hazel?” Roo murmured. He snuggled the yarn close to his cheek. It tickled his whiskers.

“Just right, Roo,” Hazel agreed, her voice low and warm. “And look. I found a little feather from a robin’s wing, soft as milk. And some fallen leaves, rustly and warm from sleeping under the sun.”

Back in their cozy burrow, a safe place under the roots of an old oak tree, they began to make the blanket. Roo used his quick little paws to work the yarn. He looped and wove. His nose was close to his work. He hummed a quiet happy tune, like a sleepy song. Hazel helped by gently pressing the fluffy seeds into the yarn, making it softer and fuller. She tucked the soft robin’s feather right in the middle, like a little treasure. They carefully layered the fallen leaves around the edge, a warm border that smelled of gentle earth and sleepy fall days. The blanket was not perfectly straight, but it was made with the warmest wishes from two dear friends.

When it was finished, it was a lovely soft blanket of warm colours. Roo carefully rolled it up, keeping its softness. Hazel, with Roo nestled safely on her soft fur, hopped out into the cool dark air. The stars were beginning to appear. They twinkled like tiny sleepy eyes opening in the dark blue sky.

They found Sion the scarecrow standing tall. His straw arms reached out, as if waiting for a hug. As they came closer, he seemed to sigh softly in the gentle breeze.

“Hello, Sion,” squeaked Roo. He held up the little blanket. The sunrise colours glowed softly.

Hazel gently placed the warm blanket over Sion’s straw shoulders. The yarn nestled against his straw body. The fluffy seeds puffed up like a cozy pillow. The little robin’s feather tickled his straw collar. Sion stood a little straighter. He could not speak with words, but they both felt a happy little rustle of his straw. It was a silent thank you.

“He looks so much warmer now, doesn’t he, Hazel?” smiled Roo. His heart felt as warm as the blanket.

Hazel nodded. Her bright eyes shone with quiet joy. “He does, little Roo. He really does. And it’s good we made it before the real cold wind comes.”

As they hopped back toward their warm safe burrow, the sky was a deep dark blue, sprinkled with a million million twinkling stars. Back in their cozy home they found two little mugs of warm chocolate drink. Mama Mouse had left them, a sweet surprise. The steam curled up, smelling sweet and warm, like a hug in a mug. They snuggled together on a bed of soft moss. They sipped their cocoa. Their hearts were full of warmth and the peaceful joy of helping a friend. The wind outside still whispered its nighttime stories, but inside their burrow all was calm and safe. Soon, with sleepy sighs and happy thoughts of Sion the scarecrow feeling warm and cozy, Roo and Hazel, nestled close together, drifted off to slumber. Their dreams were as soft and colourful as the little blanket they had made.
